title: You admire the outcome…
paragraphs:
You admire the outcome…
But you’ve ignored the process.

You quote the promotion…
But skip the pit.

You celebrate the palace…
But refuse the prison.

But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Joseph’s success was never about position.
It was about presence.
It started in silence.

A young man… betrayed by his own brothers.
Thrown into a pit. Sold like property. Forgotten like he never mattered.
And you would’ve quit there.
Be honest.

The moment life turned unfair…
The moment obedience didn’t produce comfort…
The moment God didn’t explain Himself…
You started drifting.

God saw it.
You knew.

Joseph didn’t have a Bible.
No church.
No worship band.
No “open doors.”
What he had… was God.
“The Lord was with Joseph, so he became a successful man…” — Genesis 39:2
Read that again.

Not: “Joseph was successful, so God was with him.”
No.
God’s presence came first.

In the house of Potiphar—he served with integrity.
In the face of temptation—he ran from sin.
In prison—he stayed faithful when no one was watching.

You?
You negotiate with sin when it’s convenient.
Joseph fled.
“How then can I do this great wickedness and sin against God?” — Genesis 39:9

He didn’t say, “sin against my future.”
He didn’t say, “ruin my reputation.”
He said… “against God.”
That’s the difference.

Spiritual Diagnosis:
You want Joseph’s reward…
But you’re tolerating what Joseph refused.

You want elevation…
But you’re compromising in private.

You want God to “open doors”…
While entertaining the very sin that shuts His voice.

Joseph was falsely accused.
Thrown into prison.
And here’s where most people break.
Because obedience didn’t protect him from suffering.
Let that confront you.
“But the Lord was with Joseph and showed him steadfast love…” — Genesis 39:21

In the pit—God was with him.
In slavery—God was with him.
In prison—God was with him.

So why do you think God left you…
Just because life got hard?
You misinterpreted discomfort as abandonment.
But it was development.

God wasn’t ignoring Joseph.
God was building Joseph.

Character before calling.
Purity before power.
Faithfulness before favor.
Then suddenly…

The prison becomes a pathway.
The forgotten becomes remembered.
The slave becomes ruler.
And Pharaoh says:
“Can we find a man like this, in whom is the Spirit of God?” — Genesis 41:38
That’s the real secret.

Not strategy.
Not luck.
Not connections.
The Spirit of God.
Joseph didn’t chase success.

He walked with God…
And success chased him.
Now stop.
This is your moment.
Because here’s the truth:

Joseph’s story isn’t just about success…
It’s about salvation.
You and I are not Joseph.

We are the brothers.
We are the betrayers.
We are the sinners.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
That’s you.
That’s why no amount of discipline or “being like Joseph” can save you.
But God didn’t leave you there.
He sent Jesus Christ.

Not to give you a better life…
But to give you a new one.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

Jesus took your sin.
Your compromise.
Your hidden life.
He carried it to the cross.
And He offers you something Joseph could never earn:
Grace.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works.” — Ephesians 2:8–9
So here’s the decision:

Stop chasing success.
Start surrendering to Christ.

Repent.
Turn from sin.
Trust in Jesus—not your effort.
Because the greatest “promotion” isn’t a palace…
It’s being reconciled to God.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
If this exposed something in you… don’t ignore it.
You wanted Joseph’s secret.
Now you have it.
The question is…

Will you walk with God…
Or keep pretending success without Him is enough?
